newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond spreads near three year lows.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond spreads near three year lows.

text.p: Australian bonds closed at their narrowest margin to U.S. Treasuries since February 1994 after an early burst of futures led buying saw bonds break through resistance levels.
The spread to U.S. 10-year Treasuries closed at 79 points, having traded near 75 during the day, dealers said.
There was potential for further gains in the next week or so, as the market is expecting a favourable December quarter CPI result on January 29.
However, resistance at 75 basis points was expected to be substantial.
"I guess leading into our CPI next week, it's probably going to have a bid tone versus the U.S.," one trader said. "It'll be interesting to see how we perform, once the CPI is out."
Forecasts of economists surveyed by Reuters centre on a 0.3 percent rise in the December quarter CPI, for an annual rate of 1.6 percent.
The key underlying inflation rate is seen rising 0.6 percent to be 2.2 percent higher over the previous 12 months.
That is comfortably in the bottom half of the Reserve Bank's 2-3 percent target band, and further moderation in inflation is expected, at least through the first half of 1997.
While bonds strengthened across the curve, the long end was the best performer on the day.
The futures curve closed under 100 basis points for the first time since before the release of U.S. payrolls data on January 10.
